correctness.rationale: Compact positivity permits logarithmic one-coordinate generator tests. They yield the exact prey-nullcline regression and predator-fiber harmonic law. The harmonic law expands to the nonnegative conditional defect, and the predator equation converts that defect exactly into weighted mean-square per-capita speed. Conditional orthogonality gives both variance decompositions. The prey regression forces the strict stationary ceiling x<K. Vanishing of any defect makes the corresponding coordinate speed vanish on invariant support and collapses every support trajectory to the unique positive equilibrium. The packaged checker independently verifies all pointwise algebra and the equilibrium-root sign argument.

originality.rationale: Classical Holling–Tanner literature was compared for global stability, one- and two-limit-cycle results, Hopf bifurcation structure, outbreaks, and canard cycles. The complete open 2014 same-model article contains no matching conditional, variance, average, or stationary formulation under targeted full-text searches. Direct semantic searches for the two conditional laws, harmonic prey calibration, support ceiling, and activity defects returned no same-object published result. The theorem is not a restatement of nullcline geometry: it asserts exact conditional expectations for every compact positive invariant probability measure and quantifies deviations by squared coordinate speeds.

value.rationale: The two nullclines encode the defining biological mechanisms of the Holling–Tanner oscillator: saturating prey loss and a predator carrying capacity proportional to prey. The theorem upgrades those geometric curves into exact stationary calibration laws and shows, at every predator abundance, how far mean prey must lie above the instantaneous predator carrying requirement y/gamma. That excess is not an arbitrary statistic: it is exactly a weighted mean-square predator per-capita speed. The result therefore supplies a parameter-explicit consistency test for stationary or periodic predator–prey data, applies simultaneously to the model’s one- and two-cycle regimes, and sharply separates the unique equilibrium from every genuinely oscillatory recurrent state.
